Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Steve Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; and Tom Reilly, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Steve Harlan.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices with WTI averaging around $82 per barrel. We achieved impressive milestones across our key assets, particularly in exploration and drilling where we executed our capital-efficient growth strategy with precision.

In the Permian Basin, our primary focus area with over 250,000 net acres in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins, we brought 28 wells online across three pads targeting the Second Bone Spring and Wolfcamp A formations. These featured average lateral lengths of 12,500 feet, a 15% increase from the prior quarter, thanks to refined 45-stage slickwater completions using 3,000 pounds of proppant per foot along with diverter technology to enhance cluster efficiency. The initial production rates at 30 days, or IP-30s, averaged 1,450 barrels of oil equivalent per day with a 72% oil cut, marking a 12% improvement sequentially from our Q1 Wolfcamp A performers. This uplift came from our proprietary geomechanical modeling, which cut parent-child interference by 18% via better offset well timing.

We're projecting estimated ultimate recovery, or EURs, at about 1.3 million boe per well, informed by our decline curve analyses and peer analogs such as those from Pioneer and Occidental. Standout results include the Mustang 12-4H pad in Lea County, New Mexico, where four Wolfcamp C wells delivered a combined IP-30 of 6,200 boe/d, our best in the Delaware to date. Drilling and completion costs dropped to $8.2 million per well, or roughly $650 per lateral foot, a 10% reduction quarter-over-quarter, powered by our walking rig operations with Patterson-UTI's PitPhree systems that trimmed flat time by 22%.

Our success rate held at an industry-leading 98.5% for the 52 gross operated wells we spudded this quarter, with no non-productive time events lasting over 24 hours. Shifting to the Eagle Ford, our 15-well program in the Pearsall trend across Dimmit and Webb Counties posted average IPs of 950 boe/d at 65% condensate, leveraging hybrid completions that mix 2,500 pounds per foot proppant with channel fracturing techniques. This has de-risked our 40,000-acre position, lifting EURs to 850,000 boe per well and dropping breakevens to $42 WTI, comfortably under the current forward curve.

On the international front, early progress in our Suriname Block 58 venture with TotalEnergies saw us spud the Roystonea-2 appraisal well in late June, with logs revealing 180 feet of net oil pay in premium Paleogene sands similar to the Krabdagu find nearby. Testing is on deck for Q4, potentially enabling a 50,000 boe/d tie-back to nearby FPSO setups. In the Norwegian North Sea, our 20% stake in the Rosebank field with Equinor and Suncor advanced subsea template work, keeping first oil targeted for 2026 and our portion of 2P reserves at 45 million boe.

We've amplified our edge through data-centric innovations like the ApexAI seismic inversion tool, fueled by machine learning on 15 years of petrophysical datasets, which high-graded locations and bumped success rates 5 points year-over-year while pinpointing 1,200 Midland spots with EURs over 1 million boe. Completion pilots with Halliburton's dissolvable balls have cut flowback by 36 hours, complemented by fiber-optic DTS for live frac monitoring, driving a 25% year-over-year ROCE jump to 45% at $75 WTI in the Permian.

Operational metrics highlight our edge: Permian spud-to-rig-release now averages 18 days against the industry's 22-day norm per Enverus, and we've electrified 80% of rigs using GE Vernova grid-tied units, slashing Scope 1 methane intensity to 0.15%, half the peer median, to meet EU CBAM standards.

For the back half, we're steering toward 120 to 130 gross operated wells, 70% in the Permian to sustain inventory. Our three-year inventory of 4,200 spots offers over 10 years at current activity, split evenly between Tier 1 and Tier 2 with $35 to $45 WTI breakevens. Rig count plans: five in Delaware, four in Midland, two in Eagle Ford, scalable down if WTI lingers under $70.

We're chasing bolt-on M&A in the Permian Stack for 50,000 Tier 1 Wolfcamp acres at $10,000 to $12,000 per acre from free cash flow, plus a new JV with Chevron on 30,000 Southern Delaware acres sharing E&D 50/50. Tech rollout includes autonomous drilling with Nabors FlatBot for 30% ROP gains in Bone Spring by Q4, and $50 million in CCUS pilots at Salado Draw sequestering 1 million tonnes CO2 annually for 10% recovery boost and 45Q credits.

Overall, this drilling momentum is delivering top-tier returns, setting us up to return 50% of free cash flow via buybacks and dividends even at $65 to $85 WTI. Now, I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to walk through our financial results in detail.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Steve. As Steve highlighted, we posted a strong quarter across the board. Revenue reached $2.8 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income stood at $1.0 billion, while net income came in at $750 million. We generated $900 million in free cash flow and returned $500 million to shareholders via dividends and repurchases. The balance sheet is rock-solid with $5 billion in debt and $2 billion in cash.

Diving deeper into EBITDA, we reported $1.2 billion for the quarter, a solid 32% rise from $910 million in Q3 last year, pushing trailing twelve-month EBITDA to a high of $4.8 billion, up 28% YoY. Breaking down the drivers, realized pricing was key, contributing over $350 million YoY, with our blended net at $68 per boe versus $52 prior year amid OPEC+ discipline and firm demand. WTI averaged $78, Brent $82, with a $4 spread aiding us; Permian Waha gas hit $3.50 per Mcf from negatives last year via Matterhorn Express and Waha Fractionation ramps. North Sea Brent blends netted $85 per barrel premiums.

Production climbed 8% YoY to 625,000 boe/d, 62% oil, adding $150 million; Permian D&C pushed 350,000 boe/d up 12% with 12,000-foot laterals versus 10,000, plus diverters and 4,000 lbs/ft proppant for 15% IP gains. Eagle Ford steady at 120,000 boe/d but richer NGLs from Kingsville; GoM up 5,000 boe/d via Lucius tie-back; Bakken flat at 80,000 boe/d with pad optimization.

Costs fueled $180 million more via controls: LOE down 11% to $8.20/boe on 75% water recycle through Apex Water JV slashing freshwater 40%; G&A at $1.50/boe off 5% with Palantir Foundry automating 30% permitting. DD&A edged to $18.50/boe from Permian F&D, offset by topline; hedges added $50 million with 65% 2024 oil at $70 floor collars/swaps.

Permian drove 55% EBITDA at over 25% ROCE, hedged Waha risks with 1.5 Bcf/d commitments; GoM margins $45/boe EBITDA from Winterfell FPSO; Suriname appraisal de-risking 600 MMboe but muted near-term pre-FID.

Capex $1.1 billion, 80% D&C at 2.1x returns over 1.5x hurdle; FCF $850 million funded 10% dividend to $0.55/share and $300 million buybacks. Full-year EBITDA guide $4.9-5.1 billion at $75-80 WTI, Q4 640,000 boe/d; watch Waha or Guyana delays, but 5+ year Tier 1 inventory and <1% flaring fortify us.

On production guidance, for Q4 we're at 450,000 to 470,000 boe/d, up 3-5% sequentially, oil 285,000-295,000 bbl/d (62%), NGLs 65,000-70,000 bbl/d, gas 600-650 MMcf/d, assuming no Gulf weather hits. Full-year 2024 reiterated at 1.65-1.75 million boe/d, 8-10% growth from 2023's 1.52 million, oil 1.05-1.12 million bbl/d (64%), NGLs 240,000-260,000, gas 2.3-2.5 Bcf/d; capex $2.8-3.0 billion, 70% Permian/Eagle Ford D&C.

Upside from Permian 45-50 Q4 wells at 1,800-2,200 boe/d IP with 12,000-14,000 ft laterals, ceramic proppant, 35-ft spacing; "Pioneer Pulse" for 20-25% EUR lift via fiber-optics. Permian Q4 850,000-900,000 boe/d. Eagle Ford 15-20 wells, 55-60% oil, CO2 EOR +10,000 boe/d, NETEX security. GoM 120,000-130,000 boe/d post-Neptune, Lucius +15,000 by year-end, 25% drill efficiency. Digital via Palantir/SLB Delfi for 5-7% gains, 30% less downtime.

North America 90%, differentials $1.50 under WTI; intl North Sea 40,000 boe/d, Guyana stake conservative. Risks: hurricanes (buffers), Permian turnarounds (5,000 boe/d deferral), flaring regs (we're at 92% capture). $5 WTI drop trims 2% via deferrals, 60% hedged $75 floor; inflation offset by contracts.

This supports 50% FCF yield at $70 WTI, 10+ year inventory, opportunistic M&A like $400M Martin tuck-in.

Capital allocation: post-$5.2B FCF up 25% at $82 WTI/$3.15 HH, priorities: balance sheet (0.2x leverage), returns, growth. Cumulative $12B FCF since '22, returned $8.5B.

Dividends first: 10% hike to $0.40/share quarterly ($1.60 ann.), 3.2% yield, 25% FCF payout <30-40% target; $1.1B next year, $250M variable Q3. Permian 55%, Eagle Ford 20%, GoM growth.

Buybacks: $4B auth., 18M shares (4.2%) at $145 avg., 8% EPS accretion, ROCE 18%; $1.5-2B 2025 for 3-5% reduction below $200 NAV (8.5B boe reserves), 6x EV/EBITDA value.

Reinvestment: 2025 capex $6.8B flat, 65% upstream, 20% midstream, 15% tech/transition; 5-7% growth to 1.35M boe/d, 65% oil.

Upstream: Permian $4.2B/120 wells, Waha gas capture, ApexPro 2,500 boe/d IP, electric rigs <1% flare. Eagle/Bakken $800M LNG-tied. GoM/intl $500M tie-backs/Suriname. Midstream $400M Pecos NGL. Digital $300M SLB AI 92% success; CCUS $500M 5 MMtpa Permian.

10-year $35 breakeven inventory, M&A like $1.2B Midland at 4x FCF. 40% returns/60% reinvest for 8-10% NAV CAGR.

I'll now hand off to Mike for operations.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we're firing on all cylinders. Production averaged 450,000 boe per day. We ramped up successfully with new pads like Mustang contributing meaningfully ahead. Cost initiatives advanced sharply.

Our midstream segment shone, posting $450 million adjusted EBITDA, up 12% YoY and 35% of total, from fee-based flows shielding commodity swings. Throughput hit 4.2 million boe/d equivalent, +8% YoY/+4% sequential, 10th straight growth quarter on basin ramps.

Crude pipelines record 2.1 MMbbl/d, +10% YoY; EPIC JV Permian-Gulf at 1.2 MMbbl/d 92% full, $1.05/bbl tariffs, 95% take-or-pay. Bakken Dakota 750 kbbl/d +5%. Gas 8.5 Bcf/d +3% seq., 88% util., Appalachia +15% 3.2 Bcf/d LNG, Permian 4.1 via Matterhorn, $0.28/MMBtu 92% MWAs. NGLs 850 kbbl/d +7%, Houston exports 600 kbbl/d on $0.25/gal cracks, 1.2 MMbbl/d loadings; refined 450 kbbl/d 90%.

Permian 55% volumes +12% at 300 rigs. Network 20,000 miles 89% util., $1.2B revs 42% margin.

Growth capex $2.8B/'24 ($1.5B YTD): Permian NGL +200 MMcf/d $180M underbudget, Mont Belvieu 1.1 MMbbl/d 85% contracted. Corpus Christi Phase 1 +400 kbbl/d exports 70% slotted $0.80/bbl to 4.1 MMbbl/d EIA. DAS on 40% lines -25% downtime; $50M CCS Permian 45Q.

$1.2B secured to '26 like 550 MMcf/d Permian 12-14% IRR, 90% fee-based. $25B assets 75% IG counterparties, 5-7% vol growth LNG/Permian. Q4 EBITDA $460-480M, FY +9% vols, raised total EBITDA $5.9-6.1B, 10%+ distributions.

Now over to Tom for exploration specifics.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Mike. Our exploration program holds tremendous promise. We wrapped a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware and plan 10 exploration wells next year. These could materially expand reserves, building on recent intl logs and North Sea progress Steve noted, with Suriname and Rosebank de-risking significant resources.

Operator, we're ready for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Levy with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Levy: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the key well results and future drilling plans?

Steve Harlan: Good morning, Brian. Happy to expand. Those Permian IPs and EURs we highlighted demonstrate our tech edge reducing interference and costs, with Eagle Ford de-risking and intl appraisal confirming pay. H2 rig flex and M&A/JV will sustain 10+ year inventory at low breakevens, blending returns and sustainability.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year?

Lisa Chen: Morning, Sarah. Q4 midpoint assumes Permian/Eagle Ford ramps and GoM rebound, with full-year growth from efficiencies offsetting risks like weather via hedges and buffers. Upside in tech and inventory depth keeps us on track for FCF targets.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel: Could you please provide more color on midstream performance?

Mike Rodriguez: Hi David. Volumes and expansions like EPIC/Corpus underscore connectivity, with high util. and contracts driving margins. ESG tech and JV structure position for Permian/LNG growth resiliently.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Tom Reilly: Thanks, Laura. Strong seismic and well data, plus Suriname/Rosebank, bolster inventory and intl optionality, informing capex to high-IRR Tier 1 while advancing CCUS for long-term value.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Steve Harlan for closing remarks.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we're pleased with Q3 performance. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering shareholder value. Thank you for joining today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
